summary: Cross-identity session linkage created after SCIM merge results in duplicate sessions and intermittent access to another user's console
description: Issue summary: During a user merge performed by the SCIM reconciliation job, two user identities were linked at the session layer. This produced duplicate active sessions where one session intermittently reflected the other user's RBAC claims. Impact: Affected internal staff observed seeing stale role claims (temporary elevation) or missing roles unpredictably when switching between tabs or services. No external customer data was accessible, but the behavior risks privilege confusion for oncall and SRE workflows.
impact: ~7 users intermittently affected; primarily support-console and runbook-runner access. Potential privacy/privilege risk; currently contained to prod us-west. No confirmed malicious activity.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Trigger a SCIM merge for accounts with shared external_id hashes (test clone of production data).
2) Observe session records in session-store for both identities immediately after merge (session_id reuse or linked parent_id present).
3) Login as merged user and open support-console; switch to runbook-runner in a new tab to surface claim desync.
4) Check identity-proxy request headers; some requests carry the merged user's session token but the RBAC claim payload belongs to the pre-merge identity.
5) Capture traces via X-Req-Id and correlate to scim-sync job run id.
logs_and_artifacts: Auth trace: req=abcd1234 owner=user-137 -> session parent_link=session-xyz (unexpected)
Session-store dump (redacted): session-xyz { user_id: user-137, linked_user_ids: [user-522], last_touch: 2026-03-10T14:02:11Z }
Sample console audit entry: 2026-03-10T14:04:02Z user=user-137 action=impersonation_check result=ok (claims from user-522)
hypothesis_and_investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: SCIM merge job updated identity aliasing but did not atomically update session linkage metadata, leaving stale linked_user_ids in session-store.

Identity-proxy applies RBAC claims from cached session blob when request arrives; if session blob references linked_user_ids, proxy selects highest-privilege claim without verifying primary ownership.
Reproduced locally by replaying scim-sync merge with existing sessions present; observed session.parent_link set to the wrong canonical id when merge ordering was reversed.
Race condition suspected between scim-sync worker finalize step and session-store cleanup TTL (finalize writes alias table, session cleanup expects alias table first).
temporary_workaround: Run session invalidation for affected user IDs and force re-login: /admin/sessions/invalidate?user_ids=[user-137,user-522]. Also paused SCIM merge batch processing until hotfix deploy. Issued a temporary helm rollout that disables non-critical session-link merging in scim worker.
proposed_fix: 1) Patch scim-sync to perform atomic alias swap and emit a session-invalidate event for merged user IDs. 2) Add an identity-proxy verification step: cross-check session.primary_user == claim.user before applying RBAC claims; if mismatch trigger re-auth flow. 3) Add unit+integration tests to simulate merge concurrency.
next_steps: 1) PR created: github.com/redwood/auth-service/pull/4887 (hotfix) — awaiting review by 2026-03-13.
2) Schedule canary deploy to staging and us-west-small pool on 2026-03-14.
3) Run retro-check sweep to invalidate sessions for all merges in the last 48 hours.
4) Postmortem + runbook update after incident closure.
